document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Official Says that Relations with Russia and Iran "Tense"
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Mullah Abdul Jalil tells a US political officer that relations with Russia and Iran are tense. He says the Taliban do not know where Osama Bin Laden or other "Arabs" flushed from training camps are, but are seeking Commander Masoud.

events.description: Taliban capture Kabul and Baghram airbase.
Russian government statement condemning Najibullah's execution and Kabul seizure.
UN envoy Norbert Holl meets Taliban delegation led by Mohammed Hasan in Kandahar.
Hour-long phone call between Abdul Jalil and US Embassy officer; Taliban form six-member council under Mullah Mohammed Rabbani.
Holl due to travel to Kabul to meet Mullah Mohammed Rabbani.
Earlier conversation of Jalil with US poloff denying knowledge of bin Laden's whereabouts.
Taliban capture Kabul and seize Baghram Airbase, capturing eight Sukhoi bombers and four MiG-21s.
Russian government statement condemns Najibullah's execution as barbaric and says the seizure of Kabul aggravates the crisis.
Iran radio Pashtu and Dari services announce that Iran continues to recognize Masood and Rabbani as the legitimate government.
UN envoy Holl meets a Taliban delegation led by Kandahar governor Mohammed Hasan.
Taliban form a six-member council headed by Mullah Mohammed Rabbani after seizing Kabul.
Phone conversation between Jalil and the embassy political officer on Taliban relations with Russia, Iran and bin Laden.
Holl scheduled to travel to Kabul to meet Mullah Mohammed Rabbani.
Earlier conversation between Jalil and embassy officers where he denied knowledge of bin Laden's whereabouts.

key_claims: Taliban deputy foreign affairs adviser said relations with Russia and Iran were 'tense' after the 27 Sept 1996 capture of Kabul.
Jalil denied that the Taliban knew the whereabouts of Osama bin Laden or other 'Arabs' flushed from camps; US urged no safe haven.
Taliban were pursuing Masood, who retreated to the Panjshir Valley; Baghram airbase's aircraft were captured.
Taliban said Iran harbors several thousand anti-Taliban Afghans who might invade western Afghanistan.
Taliban claimed control of over two-thirds of Afghanistan, with Mullah Omar as head of state and Kandahar the movement's capital.
Embassy noted Holl met only mid-level Taliban officials, none of the inner shura.
